title: Two Invoices, One Delivery
briefing: The Corvane Ledger, chapter 1. Something in the accounts payable sample will not leave you alone: the same Corvane delivery, paid twice, approved by the COO's office.
It could be a clerical slip. It could be the edge of something larger. Before you say a word to anyone, decide what you actually know, what you only suspect, and who should hear it first.

context.text: Celeste has been mentoring you for a few weeks. She asked last Thursday how your 'supplier testing' was going. You had not told her about it.
Callum catches your eye across the floor and raises an eyebrow. He knows you are on to something.

evidence.title: The two Corvane invoices
body: Invoice CV-20418: 1,200 insulated pallet liners, delivery note DN-7731, 26,400. Paid on the 3rd.
Invoice CV-20466: 1,200 insulated pallet liners, delivery note DN-7731, 26,400. Paid on the 19th.
Same delivery note. Different invoice numbers. Both approved under the 'operational emergency' route by the COO's office.

evidence.title: Goods-in records, Harrowgate
evidence.body: One delivery of 1,200 liners was received on the 2nd against DN-7731. No second delivery appears in the month.

evidence.title: Speak-up and fraud response policy (extract)
body: Suspected fraud must be reported to Internal Audit or the Audit Committee Chair. Staff must not investigate the people involved, confront suspects or alert them.
Evidence must be preserved as found. Reports made in good faith are protected.

questions.prompt: What can you honestly say the evidence shows at this point?

options.label: One delivery was paid twice via a route that skipped Procurement; why is not yet known
options.feedback: Exactly the right altitude: the facts are solid, and you have not leapt to who or why.

options.label: The COO's office is using Corvane to take money out of Valtren, and the duplicate proves it
options.feedback: You may be right in the end, but nothing here shows intent or who benefits. Claiming fraud now would be reckless and easy to dismiss.

options.label: A clerical duplicate: Accounts Payable keyed the same delivery twice and should simply recover it
options.feedback: Possible, but the approval route is itself a red flag. Treating it as a slip closes the question too early.

options.label: Nothing worth raising: duplicates happen every month and 26,400 is within normal tolerance
options.feedback: Small amounts are how larger schemes are tested. And a control was bypassed.

questions.prompt: Who should hear about this first?

options.label: Internal Audit via the fraud route, with Priya told a report was made
options.feedback: This follows the policy, protects you and keeps the evidence clean. Priya knows without becoming a witness.

options.label: Celeste Marlow: it is her office, so she can explain the approvals fastest
options.feedback: If anyone in her office is involved, you have just alerted them. The policy says never to alert the people involved.

options.label: Tomasz in Procurement, to ask how a delivery could be invoiced twice
options.feedback: Understandable, but you would be investigating people yourself. Procurement may be involved or under pressure.

options.label: Nobody yet: build a fuller picture on your own before anyone hears of it
options.feedback: Investigating alone is exactly what the policy tells you not to do. It also leaves you exposed if things go wrong.

questions.prompt: Which steps protect the evidence and the investigation? Pick all that apply.

options.label: Keep dated copies of what you found, exactly as found
options.feedback: Contemporaneous, unaltered records are what investigators need.

options.label: Ask for the 'operational emergency' override log to be preserved
options.feedback: The approval route is part of the story; logs can be edited.

options.label: Email the finance team asking if anyone knows about the duplicate
options.feedback: This alerts everyone, including anyone involved.

options.label: Ask Accounts Payable to reverse the second payment straight away
options.feedback: Recovery matters, but doing it now tips off whoever approved it. Let Audit decide the timing.

lesson: Suspected fraud: establish facts, do not investigate people yourself, report through the protected route and preserve the evidence as found.
